scenes.text: A bird that weighs about as much as a bar of soap flies farther every year than any other animal we know of.
It's the Arctic tern, and it weighs only around one hundred grams.
Every year it flies from the Arctic all the way to Antarctica, and back again.
In twenty ten, scientists fitted terns from Greenland and Iceland with tiny trackers weighing just over one gram.
On average, the birds flew about seventy thousand kilometers in a single year.
That's around forty-four thousand miles, the longest migration ever recorded at the time.
And they don't fly in a straight line.
They follow a giant S-shaped route, riding the planet's wind systems.
They even stop for almost a month in the middle of the North Atlantic to feed.
Arctic terns can live about thirty years.
Over a lifetime, that adds up to about two point four million kilometers.
That's like flying to the Moon and back three times.
And because they chase summer at both ends of the planet, they see two summers every year.
That means they see more daylight than any other creature on Earth.
Would you fly to the Moon and back three times for endless summer? Tell me below.

title: This tiny bird flies to the Moon and back 3 times 🐦
caption: Arctic terns fly from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year, about 70,900 km on average. Over a 30-year life, that's like 3 round trips to the Moon.
